items.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Barney Bigard was the clarinet... I said to Sid, 'Take the night off, we'll get another drummer; you go down to Symphony Hall and get those guys to come back to the club.' ... Sid was at the microphone and as they walked in the back of the club, Sid says, 'Oh here comes Barney Bigard.'

ctx.x: Then you became the music director for the Savoy for a short time. [NOTE TO KIMERY re below– George says what sounds like 'Club Sade' and 'Mrs. Donnelley', but we are talking about the Savoy and the owner was Mrs. Donahue. I think George was tongue tripping over Donahue and earlier club manager Connelly]

Well, Mrs. Donnelley who owned the Club Sade [Mrs. Donahue owned the Savoy] and I knew the musicians and why not do that. And I did that successfully. That was a good thing for about a month or two, I don't know. I brought in Vic Dickenson and I brought in Wild Bill, I brought in Joe Thomas, a wonderful trumpet player, and with local musicians, and I was playing piano. We had some good weeks there. But I think when Phil Napoleon came in with his own band and sold Mrs. Donahue the idea of having his band – which…

night. One night – and Bob Wilber as the opener – and I asked Bob but he a different kind of band. He had Wilber and Sidney de Paris and Big Sid Catlett on the drums. And of course having Big Sid there was … that was a thrill. But I mean, that band cost me a thousand dollars a week. That's a lot of money. Six guys living in New York, paying their hotels … and getting a thousand dollars a week. Maybe it wasn't a thousand, maybe it was nine hundred. items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: George Wein's idea that he'd like to reminisce... George told me, 'Get here a little early because Duke is coming in early.'

ctx.x: No, '73, I guess it must have been because he died in '74. It must have been 1973.

Well, -- which was George Wein's idea that he'd like to reminisce, you know, get a few of his men that was in the group, like Sonny, Nance, myself, and somebody else, I don't know. And so George told me, "Get here a little early because Duke is coming in early." He had been working somewhere. I don't know, it was somewhere in Jersey somewhere. And he was coming in for a rehearsal with Nance and Sonny and myself. And so I said, "Okay."

So I came in early and there he was. So he started rehearsing things that he had been playing, I mean, probably all that night. So he said, "What you want to do?" I said, "I'll do something simple." He said, "How about 'Tiger Rag'?" I said, "You must be kidding. 'Tiger Rag'. It's hard. I said simple. Don't you know what simple means?" So he said, "What?" I said, "Rose Room." I said, "Everybody knows 'Rose Room.'" So he said, "Okay." He said, "What tempo?" I said, "You know the right tempo," and I gave him the…
